[Testing] With controller telemetry disabled, `assertFirstRequest()` can return after only the initial GET trace is exported, allowing the caller to clear telemetry before the remaining initialization traces arrive. A late connect-client trace can then be mistaken for the click trace, causing intermittent failures. Wait for all three initialization traces before returning from `initializeUi()`.

replies.body: Fixed in 6c0afa301daf9278e7ad54dd1cb916e48400c2a0. `initializeUi()` now waits for all three initialization traces before returning, so the shared test cannot clear telemetry while an initialization trace is still pending. Both Vaadin 16 telemetry modes passed in the cloud run.

@copilot Fix the newly confirmed initialization-trace race in this PR directly. The previous validation attempt has ended without source changes, and Copilot review 5673075672 on head 07632d65bc94012bc876995f1242fc9a9722c012 found a specific actionable defect: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/21023#discussion_r4393201074. Keep this PR draft on its existing branch and base; do not create another PR or modify #21012.

Vaadin16Test.initializeUi performs the init GET and connectClient POST after the test's initial page GET, so setup creates three HTTP traces. In controller-telemetry-disabled mode, assertFirstRequest waits for only one trace and then returns after asserting whatever traces are already exported. AbstractVaadin14Test.processInitialRouteAndClientEvent then calls testing.clearData. If an initialization request has completed at the client but its servlet span has not yet been exported, its trace can arrive after this clear and be consumed as the subsequent click trace. Synchronize on all three initialization traces at the end of Vaadin16Test.initializeUi before returning. Use the existing testing.waitForTraces API and real request completion, not sleeps, relaxed click assertions, or filtering away unexpected traces. Preserve both telemetry modes and all existing agent-backed routing/RPC coverage. Do not refactor unrelated test code.

Run narrow formatting and the affected Vaadin16Test plus Vaadin16TestControllerTelemetry tasks, confirming actual execution. The original assignment still has an unresolved latest-dependency/controller validation gap: coding run 40566683168 records successful Vaadin 14.2/16 normal/controller runs, but failed paired vaadin14LatestTest/vaadin14LatestTestControllerTelemetry attempts and no successful modern controller variant. Investigate that remaining failure once using the actual errors, not another blind retry. Use -PtestLatestDeps=true for latest-dependency acceptance; an already installed supported JDK selected through existing repository test-toolchain controls is acceptable if dependency selection and behavior coverage stay intact. Exercise the retained modern controller browser path when feasible. Fix only defects introduced by this refactor. Do not disable tests, change supported versions, alter repository defaults/workflows, or bypass firewall/license/security restrictions. Report a precise environment blocker if that is what prevents validation.

Include concise, inspectable validation evidence in the actual trace-race fix commit message: exact validation commands, whether requested tests actually executed, their results, and the short concrete error for any blocked command. Do not make empty commits or commit generated logs. This evidence is needed because cloud Actions logs expose command summaries but not shell output, and build scans require activation. Do not edit the PR title/body or post replies or resolve review threads; the coordinator handles metadata and reviewed findings after verifying the fix. Follow the repository's rules, including not using --rerun-tasks.
